B_access_pricing.mcp_access_cost_details: Expensify states that MCP is included in Collect and Control at no additional charge. Its launch article says there is no MCP-specific seat or contract requirement; an Expensify account and compatible client are needed.
B_access_pricing.linked_software_cost: Submit is free for individuals; Collect is $5 per member per month; Control is reported as $9–$36 depending on Expensify Card adoption and billing model. Team plans have a 30-day free trial.
B_access_pricing.pricing_model_details: No MCP per-call charge or quota was found. MCP is included at no additional charge in Collect and Control.
B_access_pricing.other_access_restrictions: An active Expensify account and an MCP-compatible client are required. OAuth consent is required. Data access is described as limited to what the authorizing member can access under their account and Workspace permissions. The launch article says no admin gate is required.
B_access_pricing.restrictions_controlled_by: Expensify controls OAuth authorization and service availability; account and Workspace permissions govern accessible data; the user approves or revokes the connection.

D_server_side_logic.additional_logic:
1. The vendor documents one read-only Search tool and no write or destructive operations. Tool annotations (readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint, openWorldHint) are not published.
2. OAuth consent is required before connecting. No server-enforced per-call confirmation flow is documented; no modifying tools are documented.
3. OAuth metadata advertises mcp:tools and integrations:api. Help documentation says the MCP grant provides read access according to account and Workspace permissions. User consent and revocation are documented; token lifetime, allowlists, role inheritance details beyond those permissions, and admin switches are not specified. Marketing says no admin gate is needed.
4. No read-only URL mode, tool filters, query-free mode, sandbox, or region variants were found. Vendor materials describe read-only access at launch.
5. Docs limit access to data available to the member under account and Workspace permissions. Field masking, PII exclusions, and finer data boundaries are not documented.
6. No MCP-specific rate limits, result caps, quotas, or per-call costs were found.
7. Tool input schemas and validation/correction rules are not published. Supplied endpoint evidence showed a JSON-RPC parse error on POST; no parameter behavior could be tested from that response.
8. No MCP call audit or telemetry behavior was found. Expensify's device-management help says OAuth-MCP connections are shown in device management and can be revoked; it describes access metadata, not individual MCP calls.
9. The official documented tool is Search. No vendor feedback, rating, survey, or reporting tool is documented. The tool description is not published; no MCP-specific upsell messages were found.
10. No initialize instructions or server-delivered skill were found. Official materials provide client setup instructions and say the connected assistant performs the analysis and summarization.
11. Whether past agent use changes later outputs or available tools/resources/prompts is unknown.
12. Official materials describe a single Search tool on https://www.expensify.com/mcp. The supplied endpoint is a separate host/path with its own OAuth authorization-server metadata; no nested servers or proxy architecture are documented.
13. No raw API, arbitrary SQL, script execution, or other escape-hatch tool is documented.
behavioural_instructions_to_ai_verbatim: The MCP server provides read-only access to Expensify data through the Search tool. Your AI assistant can search, retrieve, and analyze data, but it cannot create, edit, or delete anything in Expensify.
Only the Search tool is exposed, scoped to the permissions you already have.
D_server_side_logic.server_structure_explanation: The documented product endpoint exposes Search functionality as one tool. The supplied endpoint has a different hostname and path; no evidence describes a hierarchy or proxy structure.

E_aggregated.action_count: 1 documented tool for the official documented endpoint; exact count at supplied /mcp/v1 endpoint not independently enumerated
E_aggregated.action_count_comment: An official tool list exists in Expensify's help article and blog: they identify Search as the exposed tool; neither states a numeric total. actions.json lists that one official documented tool as best-available same-product evidence because no input-endpoint tool list was found. Claude's third-party connector directory (Anthropic verified, added July 2026) and Manufact (2026-09) each list GetCurrentUser, GetWorkspaceList, and Search. Those two additional names are excluded because Expensify says only Search is exposed. Agent Discoverability lists four differently described tools for an Expensify ChatGPT plugin; this is a separate third-party surface and is not used for the hosted MCP action list.

actions.description: Search, retrieve, filter, and analyze the member's searchable Expensify data.

E_aggregated.token_method: No public server code or verbatim initialize/tool schemas were available; tool parameter schemas and initialize instructions are not published.
E_aggregated.human_can_agent_cannot: The product supports approving reports, editing expenses, reimbursing payments, and managing Workspace settings, which the vendor says the MCP cannot do. Other product functions include issuing or locking cards, paying bills, and other expense-management workflows; vendor materials specifically state the MCP cannot lock cards or move money. Sources: https://help.expensify.com/articles/new-expensify/connections/connect-ai-assistants/Use-the-Expensify-MCP-Server-With-AI-Assistants ; https://use.expensify.com/blog/expensify-mcp

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: Expensify offers example questions such as “What did I spend on travel last month?” and “Show me all expenses over $100 missing receipts.” It says these are illustrative examples, not a complete set of supported queries. The connected AI assistant, rather than the MCP server, performs analysis and summarization.
F_documentation.governance_promises: The vendor says OAuth 2.1 with PKCE is used; the user approves connections on a consent screen and can revoke access. It promises read-only access scoped to existing account permissions. The general privacy policy describes collection, use, disclosure, and retention of service data, but no MCP-specific retention period or model-training policy was found.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: Expensify says the MCP offers realtime access to searchable data, requires no manual API key, and is included in certain plans at no additional charge. It says agents cannot create, edit, delete, approve, reimburse, or move money.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: OAuth metadata corroborates the existence of an authorization server, registration, token, and revocation endpoints. Vendor materials document a read-only Search workflow, but public code, schemas, annotations, permission enforcement details, and MCP call logs were unavailable, so most implementation claims could not be independently checked against server logic.

contradictions: The supplied endpoint is https://mcp.expensify.com/mcp/v1, while current official setup material points clients to https://www.expensify.com/mcp. The hosts and paths differ; available evidence does not establish whether these are aliases or have identical tool sets.
The input's connection-test note reports HTTP 401, while the supplied pre-fetched POST response for the same endpoint is HTTP 200 with a JSON-RPC Parse error.

Official Expensify materials say only Search is exposed. The Claude connector directory and Manufact list GetCurrentUser and GetWorkspaceList as additional tools; they are excluded from actions as third-party claims that conflict with the vendor's stated tool surface.

Agent Discoverability lists AccountSummary, GetWorkspaceList, GetCurrentUser, and Search for an Expensify ChatGPT plugin. This differs from the official Search-only statement and may describe a separate plugin surface; its tools are not included.
observations_for_research: The endpoint's OAuth authorization-server metadata advertises integrations:api in addition to mcp:tools, whereas Expensify's help article describes the MCP grant as mcp:tools and read-only. The metadata does not explain whether integrations:api is available to this MCP client.
Expensify documents the server as read-only and scoped to the member's existing account and Workspace permissions; it delegates analysis and summarization to the connected AI assistant.
notes: Reviewed links.json, links_check.txt, pages/INDEX.txt, all collected official documentation pages and scripts, pricing/legal pages, and the available code inventory. No official MCP implementation repository, tool schemas, protocol version, initialize instructions, token lifetime, rate limits, data masking rules, or MCP call-log specification was found. The public Expensify/App repository listed in the collection was not identified as this hosted server's code and its local copy was unavailable. Unofficial/community implementations were found but not used as evidence. Pricing page content was sparse in the local capture; plan pricing is taken from Expensify's AI disclosure page. Endpoint-specific actions remain uncertain because the public tool list documents a different host/path.
